column2: A New York subway station wall of white ceramic tile with a green tile band and a mosaic sign that says COUNTED ST, a red LED sign that says PLEASE SWIPE AGAIN, service change notices, a yellow fare card vending machine, grime and chewing gum, a steel turnstile bar worn to a shine.

The interior wall of a New York subway car: a row of windows with black night and motion blur outside, orange and yellow plastic seats below, and above the windows a continuous strip of advertising cards: a dermatologist ad with a rainbow and a flower head that says THANK YOU DR. MLOW, an injury lawyer ad that says COUNTED AND COUNTED, a learn bartending ad, a subway map card.

A subway platform wall of white tile with a black mosaic band, and a long row of brass coat hooks with folded trousers hanging from them, each pair with a paper claim tag on string, a subway map poster, a sign that says CHECK YOUR PANTS HERE.

The Tennessee marble wall of Grand Central Terminal with its warm beige stone blocks, a brass sconce, a brass framed split flap departure board that reads DELAYED FIVE MINUTES on every line, a frozen brass clock, a gilded ticket window.

A subway station wall of white tile with a black tile band and a mosaic that says 1 AV, plastered with hand drawn tribute posters of a rat carrying a slice of pizza, candles in glass on a ledge, a bronze plaque that says HE HAD DINNER HANDLED, grime, a service change notice.

A SoHo cast iron facade painted cream with tall windows, a bakery shop window full of pastries on tiered stands, pink boxes stacked in the window, a hand lettered sign that says ONE PER PERSON, flyers, a brass plaque, a fire alarm box.

The wall of a tiny New York studio apartment: peeling cream paint over exposed brick, a silver radiator, framed rent receipts in a grid, a tiny window that looks straight into another brick wall, crowded shelves of jars and books, a folding bike hung on hooks, exposed pipes, a floor plan taped up that says 300 SQ FT.

A New York deli wall of shelves packed with soft drink cups, bottles, bags of chips, candy, gum, lottery scratch cards and a hand painted sign that says 16 OZ MAX, a glowing fridge case, a wall of cigarette boxes with blank labels, a scratched steel counter edge.

The curved granite facade of the Alexander Hamilton Custom House at Bowling Green: carved stone, tall windows, bronze lamps, a bronze plaque, a blue police barrier at the base, autumn leaves at the edge.

A Greenwich Village brick wall and a green lamppost plastered with photocopied flyers that say LOOKALIKE CONTEST, SUNDAY 1 PM, WASHINGTON SQUARE PARK, $50 PRIZE, each flyer with the same grainy flower head photo, stickers, staples, torn edges, a NO STANDING sign.

A Central Park rustic stone wall with ivy and autumn hedges, a green park sign that says THE POND, a brass railing, a birders notice board with pinned photos of a Mandarin duck and the silhouette of an eagle owl, fallen yellow leaves along the base.

The weathered rust steel wall of the High Line with wild grasses and planting at its base, a pigeon mural stencilled on the steel, a sign that says DO NOT FEED THE BIRDS covered in bird droppings, pigeons sitting on a steel ledge, old railway rails in the planting.

A Midtown bar facade in December: dark wood and brass, windows full of holiday lights and Santas inside, a chalkboard that says SANTAS WELCOME, a lost red hat on a railing, a sign that says NO PUBLIC RESTROOM, steam, a line of empty red plastic cups along the ledge.

A wall of towering Times Square LED billboards and theatre marquees, every screen showing the words NEW YORKERS, COUNTED, N3W and MLOW in bright colours with giant eye flowers, a scaffold, a news ticker, dazzling, night.

The oak panelled interior wall of New York City Hall with a framed job posting that says RAT CZAR WANTED, BLOODTHIRSTY, GENERAL AURA OF BADASSERY, a grid of wanted posters of rats with mugshot numbers, a brass plaque, a wheeled black trash bin lid mounted like a trophy, a flag.

A bodega wall of completely empty metal shelves with price tags still on them, a single loaf of bread left on one shelf, a newspaper rack with a front page that says HISTORIC, a hand written sign that says NO MORE SALT NO MORE SHOVELS, a wall clock, a fridge door.

A Coney Island boardwalk hot dog stand facade in green and yellow paint with a hand painted menu board of hot dogs, fries and lemonade, a wall of framed champion portraits with flower heads and their numbers, red white and blue bunting, a weathered wooden boardwalk rail.
